modality.title: 1. How is your electricity priced?
modality.description: Check the energy section of your bill. Fixed price: the same price per kWh at any time. Three prices: different peak, shoulder and off-peak prices. Variable: prices change hourly or at other intervals, as in PVPC or indexed contracts. A free-market contract is not necessarily fixed-price. Each group, such as Home and Car, can have its own tariff and prices. Direct PVPC queries Red Electrica without another HA integration; the sensor option uses an existing price entity.

cycle_anchor.title: Which month starts your two-month billing cycle?
cycle_anchor.description: Only for billing every two months. Enter the month in which a consumption period starts: January = 1, February = 2, etc. For a period from 15 February to 15 April, enter 2. This is not the invoice issue month.

data.billing_anchor_month: Month in which a consumption period starts (1–12)

power_unit.title: Contracted power: find the unit on your bill
power_unit.description: Energy (kWh) measures consumption; contracted power (kW) is the capacity you pay a fixed charge for. 2.0TD has two contracted power periods: P1 peak and P2 off-peak, even if energy has three prices or uses PVPC. Find the power section and select the price unit. Do not use sensor readings in W or the total line amount.

data.power_price_unit: How is the power price expressed in your bill or contract?

power.title: Contracted power and fixed charges
power.description: Copy the bill values, not sensor readings. P1 is contracted power for peak and shoulder hours; P2 is for off-peak hours. Both may be 4.6 kW: repeat the value if your contract says so. These are not the three energy prices. Power prices in this step use {power_price_unit}, before tax. Charges accrue through today inclusive. Do not enter zero for an unknown value, as this would underestimate costs.

data.power_p1_eur_per_kw_day: Power price P1 before tax (previously selected unit)
data.power_p2_eur_per_kw_day: Power price P2 before tax (previously selected unit)

data_description.power_p1_kw: Find Contract details or Contracted power. Example: 4.6 kW. This is neither consumption in kWh nor instantaneous power in W.
data_description.power_p2_kw: Copy the off-peak contracted power. It can differ from P1; it cannot be inferred from sensors.
data_description.power_p1_eur_per_kw_day: Unit price for P1, not its total amount. Use the unit selected in the previous step.
data_description.power_p2_eur_per_kw_day: Unit price for P2. Do not enter the energy price in €/kWh here.
data_description.meter_rental_daily: If the bill only gives the rental total, divide it by the billed days. Use zero only if rental is genuinely free.

advanced.title: Advanced measurement settings
advanced.description: Keep the defaults unless you need to change them. Time allocation estimates when a Wh/kWh increment crossing prices was consumed. Set the W/kW timeout to match the device reporting frequency. This does not change contracted power or tariff type.

data.approximate_intervals: Allow estimated time allocation when a counter crosses prices
data.power_max_age_minutes: Stop integrating W/kW after this time without reports (minutes)

contract.title: Contract name and billing period
contract.description: Choose a name and the consumption period on your bill. The start day is the consumption start, not the payment day. If your supplier varies dates, you can later close an actual date range manually. Prices and contracted power are configured separately. Changes to the billing calendar take effect after the current cycle ends.

data.billing_months: Are you billed monthly or every two months?

menu.title: Configure contract
menu.description: Choose the modules you need. You can return to these options after saving.

menu_options.power_unit: Contracted power and rental (from your bill)

group.title: Group consumption and tariff
group.description: Select one or more W/kW or Wh/kWh sensors. Units are detected automatically and may be combined. W/kW is converted to estimated energy using the last known power until its timeout; no helper is required. Do not select both power and a derived energy counter for the same circuit. Each group has its own tariff. Changing sensors or tariffs preserves accrued consumption in the same invoice. A new counter waits for a genuine baseline report; groups without measurements remain unknown.

extras.title: Optional charges
extras.description: Leave unused modules at zero. Service tax is configured separately from energy tax. Export compensation requires a separate export counter and a monthly cycle; use the agreed price, capped at the value of imported energy. This does not enable virtual batteries or social tariff eligibility.

data.daily_fee_electricity_taxable: The daily charge is subject to electricity tax

finish.title: Review configuration
finish.description: Correct the indicated problem. Continue to return to the menu without losing changes.

tariff.title: Group prices
tariff.description: Direct PVPC downloads Red Electrica hourly FEU prices before tax for mainland Spain/Balearic Islands, without another integration or a price sensor. Internet is required; published hours are cached and missing hours are never extrapolated. For other modes, enter pre-tax prices or select a complete contractual price entity, not OMIE alone. Counter readings crossing different prices require consent to partial time allocation.

fiscal.title: Taxes on your invoice
fiscal.description: Enter tax percentages, not euro amounts. Values are manual, remain until you change them and need no Internet. Review suggested values; they are not updated automatically. Saving applies them to the open invoice. Closed invoices retain their breakdown.

data.tax_rules_confirmed: I checked these values against my bill or contract

data_description.tax_electricity_percent: Percentage on the electricity tax line, for example 5.11269632, not the amount charged.
data_description.tax_indirect_percent: VAT percentage on your bill. For example, 21 means 21%, not 0.21. It is added to pre-tax prices.
data_description.tax_minimum_eur_mwh: The larger of the percentage calculation and this energy minimum applies. 1 €/MWh equals 0.001 €/kWh. Check the applicable minimum; use zero only if appropriate.
data_description.tax_rules_confirmed: You are responsible for these manually configured percentages and minimum. They can be edited later.

error.whole_number: Enter a whole number within the indicated range; decimals are not accepted.
error.empty_group: A group needs a name and at least one counter.
error.source_overlap: The same sensor cannot be added and subtracted within one group.
error.invalid_units: Select existing sensors with W, kW, Wh or kWh units. Units are not inferred from names.
error.missing_price_entity: Select a price entity for the variable tariff.
error.invalid_price_units: The entity must use €/kWh, EUR/kWh, €/MWh or EUR/MWh.
error.missing_groups: Add at least one group before saving.
error.duplicate_sources: Groups would bill the same energy more than once. Check additions and subtractions.
error.invalid_surplus: Compensation requires a monthly cycle and a separate W/kW or Wh/kWh export sensor.
error.invalid_tax_profile: Review and confirm taxes. Percentages must be between 0 and 100 and the minimum cannot be negative.

missing_fiscal_rule.title: Verified tax rule missing
missing_fiscal_rule.description: The estimate is unavailable because no verified tax rule covers the invoice tax point. Update the integration or configure a documented manual profile in the contract options. Do not guess percentages based on an unresolved conditional measure.

manual_taxes_required.title: Confirm your contract taxes
manual_taxes_required.description: Measurements and closed invoices are preserved. Open Luz en Cifras → Configure → Invoice taxes, review percentages and minimum, confirm and save. This confirmation is needed once when converting the old automatic mode. Values then remain until you change them.
